messages:
emily: Heads-up — noticed a big cost spike this week on GPU jobs. Most traffic is on spot nodes in the mixed pool. Thinking about shifting to weighted scheduling between spot/dedicated rather than pure fallback. Any obvious pitfalls?

kai: +1. Are we seeing more interruptions or just longer queueing because CA can't pick up dedicated fast enough?

emily: Interruptions up ~18% last 48h (spot eviction logs), and CA latency to scale dedicated is ~90s on average which pushes some batches into timeout.

samir: One approach we've used: give a weighted capacity score per node group and have the scheduler or an admission controller prefer lower-cost groups but with a SLA penalty threshold. If latency > X, route to higher-tier. That reduces thrash.

jordan: Could we implement weighting via node labels + a scheduler plugin that prefers nodes with label `pool=cheap` but falls back to `pool=dedicated` after N seconds? Simpler: use nodeAffinity and a mutating webhook to set podAffinityPriority.

emily: I like the mutating webhook idea. But worried about rollout complexity and edgecases with daemonsets. Also need to respect taints/tolerations.

megan: For taints we already have `spot=true:NoSchedule` on spot groups. Workloads that can handle interruption have tolerations. But many batch jobs don't declare tolerations properly, so they end up stuck or scheduled onto dedicated anyway.

kai: Two operational knobs that helped us: 1) cluster-autoscaler expander set to `least-waste` and 2) a tiny warm-pool of dedicated gpus for quick absorb. Warm pool = 2-4 GPUs per AZ.

samir: +1 for warm pool. Also add a lifecycle hook for spot drain: intercept termination notice, mark node cordoned + taint `preempting=true:NoSchedule` and call a scale-up on the dedicated pool immediately. That gives CA a clearer signal.

emily: Can you sketch what that hook looks like?

samir: Sure — pseudo-scripts:

```
# on termination notice
kubectl label node $NODE preempting=true --overwrite
kubectl taint nodes $NODE preempting=true:NoSchedule --overwrite
# evict lower-priority pods with grace
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
# hit scale API for dedicated group
curl -X POST $INTERNAL_API/scale?group=dedicated&delta=2
```

jordan: Also consider using `tolerationSeconds` on the tolerant pods to allow short-lived preemption while they finish current batch instead of immediate eviction. Example toleration: `tolerations:
  - key: "spot"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
    tolerationSeconds: 120`

megan: We should be careful: `tolerationSeconds` only works for taint-based evictions, not for node drain via `kubectl drain` which forcibly evicts. So if we rely on drain hooks we should avoid forced eviction for tolerant jobs — let them gracefully finish if within budget.

kai: Another thing — CA scale-up delay is often caused by insufficient resource requests. For GPU jobs make sure we set `resources.requests: nvidia.com/gpu: 1` so CA can calculate properly. Also `--scale-up-unneeded-time` was set low for us (30s) which helped.

emily: Ops question: how do we measure the economic tradeoff? I want a rule that says "if probability of interruption > 25% and latency penalty > 200ms then use dedicated".

samir: We built a tiny metric: expected cost per successful token = (spot_cost * (1 - p_interrupt) + (fallback_cost + requeue_cost) * p_interrupt). If expected cost > dedicated_cost then dedicate. We computed p_interrupt from recent windowed eviction rate.

jordan: Can we compute p_interrupt per-AZ? We saw some AZs are much noisier. Weighting the scheduler by AZ score helps reduce cross-AZ fallback.

megan: Also add a soft quota: prefer scheduling onto spot until 70% of the pool is used, then switch to dedicated to avoid thrash when spots are scarce. This meshes with autoscaler priority buckets.

opsbot: [bot] Metric alert muted: `gpu_spot_evictions` increased to 18% in the last 12h. Runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/spot-evictions

emily: Action items from thread: 1) samir to prototype termination hook + scale API, 2) megan to audit tolerations across batch jobs, 3) kai to tune CA flags and warm-pool sizing, 4) jordan to prototype mutating webhook for affinity weighting.

samir: I'll put a small PoC in `infra/spot-fallback` today and post results.

jordan: I'll sketch the webhook — it can inject `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` for `nodeAffinity` with weight based on `spec.priorityClassName` so higher-priority pods bias to dedicated.

emily: Cool — let's sync tomorrow 10am to review PoC. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

megan: One more note: add a Canary that flips a percentage of jobs to dedicated for 1h to validate latency improvements before global change.

emily: Good call, will add to the agenda.
